title: Thresholding Error Bounded by Squared Uniform Norm
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube, and let $g$ be a real-valued function on that cube. The relative Hamming distance between $f$ and the function obtained by thresholding $g$ at zero (assigning zero the sign $+1$) is at most the square of the uniform $L^2$ norm of the difference between the real-valued version of $f$ and $g$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
